It was in response to Tata Sons' October 6 communication seeking RBI guidance on compliance with regulations.135906993“While specific guidance has not been sought on any particular regulation/ guideline/ direction, from the discussion in the board regarding listing, it seems the guidance is perhaps with respect to the same,” RBI said in its letter. “You are advised to comply with all applicable regulations/ guidelines/ directions, issued by RBI in respect of NBFCs in the upper layer (NBFC-UL), as stipulated in extant regulations/ guidelines/ directions hosted on the RBI's website, including the requirement of listing by your company.”Also Read: Jimmy Tata accuses Noel of 'back-door takeover' of Tata SonsThe latest communication leaves little room for ambiguity on the central bank's position that Tata Sons is required to list.“In case any other specific clarification is required in respect of any regulation/ guideline/ direction issued by RBI, the same may be communicated to us along with relevant details,” the central bank said.RBI did not respond to ET’s request for comment.In an earlier communication on September 11, the central bank had rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its certificate of registration as a CIC.Total Assets Over ThresholdThe central bank had directed the company to comply fully with the NBFC-UL regulatory framework.Tata Sons had applied for the voluntary surrender of its registration on March 28, 2024, after repaying all its debt. It sought to be classified as an unregistered CIC, which would have taken it outside the scale-based regulatory framework governing upper-layer NBFCs.Also Read: ET Exclusive: Jimmy Tata breaks silence on Tata matters; Backs Chandra staying chair & Tata Sons listing, opposing Noel's stanceHowever, RBI rules allow deregistration only by entities that do not hold public funds, have no customer interface and possess assets of less than 1,000 crore. Tata Sons had total assets of 2.01 lakh crore as of March 31, more than twice the 1 lakh crore asset threshold set by the RBI for classifying an entity as an upper-layer NBFC.Tata Sons has been included in the upper layer since 2022. RBI rules also provide that an NBFC placed in this category will remain subject to the stricter regulatory framework for at least five years, even if it subsequently ceases to meet the classification criteria.Tata Trusts, which controls about 66% of Tata Sons through the Sir Ratan Tata Trust and the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, wanted to avoid listing and had passed a resolution in July 2025 seeking to keep the holding company private.A listing would provide liquidity to the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which owns about 18% of Tata Sons. The debt-laden group has been seeking to monetise part of its holding to repay a portion of its estimated 60,000 crore debt.The Tata Trusts have floated a plan backed by chairman Noel Tata aimed at keeping Tata Sons privately held. This proposes the merger of Tata Electronics Systems Solutions and Tata Consulting Engineers with Tata Sons to increase operating income and take it outside the NBFC and CIC regulatory definitions, allowing it to avoid a stock market listing, which Noel Tata opposes.
